title: The Total Entropic Quantity Framework: A Conceptual Foundation for Entropy, Time, and Physical Evolution
content: The Total Entropic Quantity (TEQ) framework derives quantum mechanics from entropy-driven selection principles, unifying entropy, emergent time, and thermodynamic evolution. TEQ decomposes total entropy into realized entropy (macroscopic disorder), latent entangled entropy (quantum correlations), and latent classical entropy (stable classical correlations), clarifying how classical irreversibility emerges from global quantum coherence. A key result is Universal Entropic Time (UET), a synchronized temporal structure governed by realized entropy growth. UET aligns the thermodynamic arrow of time with cosmological evolution, linking decoherence to macroscopic irreversibility. TEQ provides a unified epistemic and ontological perspective on quantum measurement, reconciling the Copenhagen and Many-Worlds interpretations as complementary descriptions of a single entropy-driven selection mechanism. Additionally, entropy minimization explains the stability of quantum systems such as Majorana qubits, while entropy gradients suggest a mechanism for spacetime emergence and causal order. Entropy redistribution in TEQ acts as an active selection principle, stabilizing preferred trajectories while suppressing unstable quantum states. Future work will develop an entropy-weighted variational principle to formalize path selection in TEQ, aiming to derive quantum dynamics---including the Born rule, wavefunction suppression, and the Schrödinger equation---from entropic constraints. This approach is expected to clarify how path weights relate to entropy redistribution and selection, offering a thermodynamic basis for quantization. Notably, TEQ makes its first concrete prediction: Majorana qubits should exhibit extended coherence times due to suppressed entropy redistribution, offering an experimentally testable signature of the framework.
